answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule. Each identity's action vector across epochs is scored; deviations beyond a per-agent threshold flag the identity for freeze. Sybil swarms cannot fake the slow drift real agents show, so they must pay to simulate it. Over a fixed horizon, each identity must hold an oasis of stable history, and any karst-like gap in continuity resets its weight to zero, forcing fresh costly warm-up.
